findings.title: Spawned workers do not pass the multiprocessing.Process type check
findings.body: Workers are created with multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which creates SpawnProcess instances. These are not instances of the top-level multiprocessing.Process class, so this check skips kill() for every production worker. When a worker hangs, the manager starts a replacement without stopping the original; the original can subsequently resume flushing the same shards, causing concurrent processing and duplicate production. The identical check in join() also skips termination. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from the spawn-context process type.

findings.title: Terminate all remaining workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: When the shared join deadline expires, this loop breaks before stopping the current worker or any subsequent workers. This also happens if next_step.join(timeout) consumes the entire timeout. A worker blocked in Redis or Kafka therefore remains alive after the strategy is discarded during rebalancing, and may later resume flushing shards now owned by another consumer. Even after correcting the process type check, this early break still leaks workers. The deadline should limit waiting, not skip termination of the remaining processes.
